# AGENTS.md

**Before you grep, glob or open a source file: read `HANDOFF.md`, then
`docs/features/README.md`, then only the feature page(s) for the area you are
about to change. The feature pages name the files, functions and tests you
would otherwise hunt for — the code comes after them, not before.**

mega-skillstate is a plugin for the OpenCode 2.0 CLI (TypeScript, ESM) that
bounds the context window by replacing an append-only conversation history with an
explicit, structured skill-execution state (Σ) — the SKILL.state approach, derived
from the paper in `docs/arXiv-2608.26263v2/`.

Three kinds of document, and keeping them apart is the point:

- **`docs/SPEC.md` is product behavior** — what the product does and what a
  user sees, readable without knowing the code. Behavior belongs there even
  when the code is where the reason for it lives.
- **`docs/features/` is the feature map** — one page per feature with its
  files, mechanisms, traps and pinning tests. Read the page for the area you
  are about to change; keep it true in the same commit.
- **This file is process and hard rules** — the commands, the workflow and
  the constraints that apply across every feature.

Where a rule has a behavior half and a mechanism half, the behavior half is a
pointer to `docs/SPEC.md` and the mechanism half to its feature page rather
than a second copy: two copies of a default value is one more thing that can
be wrong.

## Read first
`HANDOFF.md` holds the current state; if it is missing, carry on with the
feature map and the code. Then `docs/features/README.md` — the feature map —
and only the feature doc(s) for what you are about to change.
`docs/SPEC.md` is user-visible behavior; this file is process and hard rules;
the feature docs are the map, the mechanism and the traps.

## Layout

- **The plugin package is this repo root** — `src/`, `scripts/`, `server.ts`,
  `options.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and the three package documents sit
  at the top level; the package was flattened here on `2026-10-10` and the nested
  `package.json` subdirectory it used to live in is gone. Its three documents
  are kept apart on purpose: the implementer-facing contract (`DESIGN.md`) names the
  separations and invariants for whoever edits it; `README.md` is for a user installing
  it; `docs/SPEC.md` is user-visible behaviour with no code. Merging them would force one
  audience to read another's detail.
  - `server.ts` — the host entry. The loader resolves `<plugin-root>/server`
    before `<plugin-root>/index` (`.ts` before `.js`), so a directory install
    needs only this one re-export; it points at the adapter, not the core.
  - `src/core/` — the host-free core: `schema.ts` (the schema plus the `⊕`
    merge — a `null` value deletes a key; unknown keys are dropped),
    `state.ts` (the per-session Σ store), `seed.ts` (the deterministic seed),
    `view.ts` (safe-cut helpers — turn numbering, tool-call/result pairing
    balance — ported from the live reference plugin; the pairing arithmetic is
    not reinvented here), `prompts.ts`, `compaction.ts`, `config.ts`,
    `types.ts` (the message vocabulary), and `ports.ts` (the six port
    interfaces a host adapter implements). **No host import lives in here.**
  - `src/adapters/opencode/` — the OpenCode adapter, the half that knows about
    the host: `index.ts` (`setup()`: registers the `context` and `compaction`
    hooks, the `skill_state` tool and the `/skillstate` command, and returns
    the disposer), `context.ts` (the transform — inject Σ, collapse the
    superseded prefix, seed, nudge; the heart of the plugin), `tool.ts`,
    `command.ts`, `types.ts` (the hand-written host mirror), `config.ts` (the
    host-shaped user-config path). The layering rule: the core never imports
    an adapter, and an adapter imports the core freely.
  - `scripts/smoke.mjs` — the pinning test for the hard rules below;
    `fixtures/golden.json` (captured by `scripts/capture-golden.mjs`) is the
    byte-for-byte payload baseline its golden replay section reads.
- `docs/arXiv-2608.26263v2/` — the source paper (LaTeX) the approach is
  derived from. **Read-only reference.** This repo implements the paper's
  context-window idea; it does not re-verify the paper.
- `docs/features/` — the feature map (this workflow).
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` — the forward-looking plan (portability phases, gates and
  decisions). A plan, not a description of what the code does today; the feature
  map remains the working documentation.
- `HANDOFF.md` — volatile session state; refreshed at handover, allowed to lag
  the tip (its header says the code wins).

## Commands

Everything runs from the repo root unless said otherwise.

- Install dependencies: `npm install`
- Typecheck (build gate, strict, no emit): `npm run typecheck`  (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- Smoke test (the pinning test — Σ injection, safe collapse, idempotence, merge
  semantics): `npm run smoke`  (`node scripts/smoke.mjs .`)
- Load the plugin in OpenCode: the host resolves `<plugin-root>/server`, so point
  a discovery directory at this package. Project scope:
  `.opencode/plugin/mega-skillstate`; user scope:
  `C:\Users\mega\.config\opencode\plugins\`. No build step — the host loads the
  TypeScript source directly.

The gate before a commit is every check, not just the tests:

    npm run typecheck  →  npm run smoke        (run from the repo root)

There is no separate formatter or linter yet; `tsc --noEmit` under
`strict: true` is the strict flag the smoke test runs after. A smoke run alone
will import and execute a module that still fails strict typecheck, so the
typecheck is part of the gate rather than a nicety.

## Workflow
- **The features map is part of the change, not the cleanup.** Before staging a
  commit, update the feature doc(s) for whatever you changed
  (`docs/features/`), and add an index row if the doc is new. User-visible
  behavior also updates `docs/SPEC.md` in the same commit. A docs-only
  follow-up commit is the one that gets skipped. Pure refactors with no
  behavior, mechanism, config or test change need no doc edit — do not churn
  the map.
- **Read the map before the code, and keep the map worth reading.** A feature
  page is an anti-hunting payload: the file, type, function and test names for
  one area, and the traps that cost someone an afternoon. Opening the source
  first and writing the page afterwards spends the tokens twice. If a page is
  wrong, fix it in the same commit rather than working around it — a map
  nobody trusts is worse than no map.
- **Search the map in the same breath as the code.** A grep for a feature, a
  symbol or a behaviour runs over `docs/features/` too: the feature pages name
  the identifiers and the tests, so the page you need is usually one hop from
  the hit.
- **`HANDOFF.md` is refreshed at the end of a session, not per commit.** It
  carries what only the passing session knows — open threads, next steps, the
  last thing delivered — under an `As of` stamp. It is allowed to lag the tip:
  its header says the code wins. Refresh it before you hand the work over.
- **Measure, don't deduce it.** Reading the code and doing the arithmetic in
  your head is how geometry, layout and formatting bugs ship. Print the real
  numbers from the real thing — a headless run, a scratch script, the actual
  command — and assert both the good and the broken case, so each test carries
  its own failure mode.
- **Gate on the whole check set, not just the tests.** The linter catches the
  classes of defect the test run compiles straight past. Run the formatting,
  the lint with warnings denied, the tests and the build before you call
  something done.
- **Commit messages go through a file.** Write the message to a scratch file
  (this machine uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\opencode\<project>-commit-msg.txt`)
  and run `git commit -F <path>`; a PowerShell here-string gets its terminator
  mangled by the shell tool.
- **No AI attribution in a commit message, ever, without being asked.** No
  `Co-Authored-By` trailer, no `Generated with` footer, nothing that reads as
  crediting a model or tool. These commits are the user's. This is enforced,
  not merely preferred: a machine-wide `commit-msg` hook
  (`core.hooksPath` = `C:/Users/mega/.githooks`) rejects the commit outright,
  and it blocks human co-authors too, so the only ways past it are `--no-verify`
  or `ALLOW_COAUTHOR=1`. **Use neither without the user asking in that
  conversation.** If the hook blocks something, report it and stop; do not
  reword the message to slip a trailer past the pattern.
- **Package after committing.** If the version is derived from the commit
  (a count since a base tag, a stamped build number), packaging first yields
  the previous commit's number. Raise the minor and the base together, in the
  same commit, and keep every reader of that number reading it from one place.
- **Do not commit before the user has looked at it.** Hand a visual change over
  as a build and wait for confirmation.

## Where the working knowledge lives

The per-feature working knowledge lives in `docs/features/`; its `README.md` is
the index. This file keeps the process rules and the hard rules that apply
across features; the feature pages keep the maps, mechanisms and traps.

## Hard rules

- **The context pass never mutates the durable transcript.** It only rewrites the
  outbound payload (`event.messages` / `event.system`) one action boundary at a
  time, and re-applies from scratch on every request because the host rebuilds the
  raw transcript each time. *Reason:* mutating the transcript corrupts the very
  session the transform only summarises. *Pinned by:* the smoke test's idempotence
  assertion — running the transform twice yields the identical payload.
- **Never split a tool call from its result, and never inject while a call is open
  at the tail.** Collapse happens only at safe turn boundaries from `balanceCuts`
  (`src/core/view.ts`); a state or notice message is appended only when `inFlight === 0`.
  *Reason:* the host must pair every `tool-call` with its `tool-result`; a cut or
  insert between them makes the host invent a result and the model then see two
  answers for one call. *Pinned by:* the smoke assertion that no call/result pair is
  split.
- **The runtime owns the schema, not the model.** The `⊕` merge (`src/core/schema.ts`)
  deletes a key when the patch sets it to `null`, drops keys not in the schema, and
  replaces arrays wholesale. *Reason:* the paper's failure modes are the model
  dropping or overwriting existing keys; schema ownership in the deterministic
  runtime is what keeps a malformed patch from corrupting Σ. *Pinned by:* the merge
  unit test (null-delete, unknown-key-drop).
- **The product is the repo root.** Only `docs/` and the untracked paper are not
  deployed, and never edit the reference plugin** at
  `C:\Users\mega\.config\opencode\plugins\opencode-feature-map-as-context`.
  *Reason:* that plugin is a live dependency of this host and the measured ground
  truth for the plugin API; changing it silently changes both. *Pinned by:* review
  only — there is no automated check, so treat it as a review gate.

- The README is for users. Implementation detail belongs in `docs/SPEC.md` for
  behavior and here for working knowledge, and the user must be consulted
  before technical detail is added to the README.

# skill_state tool & /skillstate command

Status: shipped (v0.2) · Read when: the model updating Σ; `state_patch`; the ack a tool returns; a tool that is registered but never called; `/skillstate`; forcing a collapse; the stale reminder.

User-visible behavior: `docs/SPEC.md` → Compaction (the seam this feeds).

## What it does

- **`skill_state`** — the tool the model calls to write Σ. Input is a `state_patch` (JSON
  mutations; `null` deletes a key) plus optional `step`. The patch is an object, or a JSON
  string the runtime decodes to one — the host's pre-`execute` validation is a hard gate, so
  the string form is admitted by the schema and parsed by the tool (see the trap below). The
  runtime merges it (⊕, unknown keys dropped) and returns a compact ack naming what changed,
  what it dropped, and whether a string had to be parsed. No reply to the user is generated
  by a state write.
- **`skill_state` with `recall`** — the same tool's read half. Passing `recall` with a key
  prints that key in full out of the session archive (or as it stands, for a key Σ still
  holds), and `recall` as the word `archive` lists what the fold set aside, largest first.
  A recall performs no write, advances no step and persists nothing, so it costs no more
  than its own reply, and — like the command — it needs no live payload, because it answers
  from the durable record. The two halves are never combined: a call carrying both is
  refused by name (see the trap in *How & why*).
- **`/skillstate`** — prints the current Σ, the measured context, and a per-turn index of
  what is collapsed vs kept; **`/skillstate now`** forces a collapse on the current pass.
  When Σ's own render has grown past `sigmaWarnTokens` the report says so, names the
  dominant key and — once the fold has run — names the archive and the command that reads
  it, because Σ is injected into every request and the collapse is indifferent to how much
  that costs.
- **`/skillstate <key>`** — prints one finding in full out of the session **archive**, which
  is where the fold puts what leaves the render. A folded key comes back whole (the render
  keeps only its head and tail), a superseded key says Σ no longer holds it, a key still live
  in Σ is printed as it stands, and a miss names the near matches. **`/skillstate archive`**
  lists what was set aside, largest first, marking the keys Σ no longer holds. Neither job
  needs the live payload, so both answer in a session no request has reached yet.
- A **standing policy** section tells the model Σ is the record and anything not written to it
  goes with the turn that knew it; plus a **stale reminder** after `staleAfter` steps with no
  new user message (only at a balanced tail).

## Map

- `src/core/skill-state.ts` — the host-free write semantics and tool vocabulary: `TOOL_NAME = "skill_state"`, `TOOL_INPUT` (the parameter contract, a union-typed `state_patch` so a quoted string is decoded rather than refused at the host's gate, plus the optional `recall` that turns the call into a read), `TOOL_OUTPUT`, `skillStateDescription`, `sessionIdOf`, `textResult`, `parsePatch`/`unfence`/`describe` (the tolerant read of `state_patch`), `writeSkillState` (parse, validate `step`/`summary` **before** the store is opened, ⊕ the patch, handle `Σ.step`, persist, return the text ack and structured output) and `runSkillState` — the dispatcher: `recall` absent goes to the write, `recall` present to the read half, which reuses the command's `recallAsk`/`recallReport`/`archiveReport` and opens nothing else.
- `src/core/sigma-condense.ts` — the fold that answers the size line, host-free:
  `condense(findings, archive, { maxChars })` → `{ findings, archive, report }`, with
  `correctedKey` (a closed suffix list, never a prefix — that would merge two different
  lessons that share a first word), `seriesStem` (numbered variants, three members
  minimum), `foldedFindingText` (head + marker + tail, the marker charged to the budget)
  and `boundedArchive` (`MAX_ARCHIVE_CHARS`, oldest out first, the newest entry never the
  one dropped). `writeSkillState` is its only caller, through `condensePast`.
- `src/adapters/opencode/tool.ts` — `createSkillState({ storage, config })` only: the OpenCode envelope (`options: { codemode: false }`, a permissive `output`, the measured details above) whose `execute` maps args to `SkillStateWrite` (including `recall`), awaits `runSkillState`, and wraps the result with `textResult`. No call logic remains here; it re-exports the core names.
- `src/core/skill-state-command.ts` — the command's host-free half: `stateBlock`, `turnIndex`, `stateReport` (read a `ContextDescriptor`), the reply phrasings `forcedReport`, `nothingYetReport`, `NOW_HINT`, `COMMAND_NAME = "skillstate"`, and the read path — `parseAsk` (the argument words, shared by both hosts), `recordFor` (the record reached from `deps` rather than from a payload), `recallReport`, `archiveReport`, and `recallAsk` (the tool's `recall` argument, so the reserved word `archive` has exactly one home). `StateView` is what the command needs from a record, `archive()` included.
- `src/adapters/opencode/command.ts` — `createSkillStateCommand({ deps, payloadOf, reply })` only: it reads `invocation.prompt.text` (`now` means force), looks up the live payload, and answers through the injected `reply` channel. It is the seam a second adapter replaces — Pi takes a **string** arg and answers through `ctx.ui.notify`.
- `src/core/prompts.ts` — `SECTION_TEXT` (policy), `stateMessageText`, `nudgeText`,
  `toolDescription`, `schemaText`, `ackText` (the ack format).
- `src/core/config.ts` — `resolveOptions` (reads `options.json` and `ctx.options`), `resolveConfig`
  (strict: unknown keys throw), `resolveThresholds`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- `src/adapters/opencode/config.ts` — `userConfigPath()`, `ensureUserConfig()`,
  `USER_CONFIG_FILENAME`, `USER_CONFIG_ENV` — the host-shaped half (where the user-level file
  sits); the rest of the config machinery is `src/core/config.ts`.
- `src/adapters/opencode/index.ts` — registers the tool **and** the command; wires the `payloads` map and
  `ctx.storage` into both, so a `/skillstate now` pass is durable too.
- `scripts/install.ts` — the installer: `parseArgs`, `packageRoot`, `userPluginDir`,
  `projectPluginDir`, `discoveryDirs`, `isLink`, `installInto`, `uninstallFrom`, `run`,
  `statusLines`. Three modes (`--project`, `--remove`, `--status`) over one script.
  The discovery-directory name is **read from `package.json` by `packageName(root)`**, never
  written again — a rename is a one-line change to the manifest, not a hunt through four
  call sites.

## How & why

- **The ack is a feedback loop, not a courtesy.** It lists `changed:` keys and
  `dropped (not in the schema):` keys, so the model learns the schema from its own writes and
  stops trying to set keys the runtime will drop. It reads the report off the context pass, so
  the numbers match what the model just saw.
- **Trap — the host validates a call before `execute`, so `TOOL_INPUT` is the gate.** A
  patch quoted as a JSON string (`"{\"files\": ...}"`) is refused host-side with
  `Invalid arguments for tool "skill_state": - state_patch: Expected object` and never
  reaches the plugin; the plugin's own guard is only the second line. `state_patch` is
  therefore declared `["object", "string"]` (the host's schema conversion accepts type
  arrays) and `parsePatch` unfences and decodes the string, refusing anything not ultimately
  an object with a soft error that names what arrived. A whole session once looped on that
  refusal, retrying smaller patches, because the message read like a size problem; with the
  union the call lands and the ack reports the parse.
- **The read half is additive, so the host gate never sees a mixed call.** `TOOL_INPUT`
  declares no `required` array, so a recall-only call passes the host's pre-`execute`
  validation untouched and the either-or rule is enforced inside `execute` instead: a call
  carrying both is refused by name rather than silently granted whichever half happened to
  be checked first. That is also why adding `recall` moved none of the tools bytes the
  golden fixtures pin — the fixtures' tools field is the bare name list, and only the
  state-message footer had to be re-captured.
- **A state write is durable.** The tool's `execute` loads through `stateStore` (cache first,
  then `storage.get`) and `apply` writes through, so the write outlives the request it came
  from — and the collapse and compaction seams see it on the same pass.
- **`/skillstate now` is a forced pass, not a bypass.** It skips only the `min`-turn gate; the
  safe-cut rules, the protected head and the balanced-tail rule still apply. It orchestrates
  `applyTransform` directly and replies with the measured numbers.
- **Two hard-won registration facts.** A tool must be added **both** at the registry
  (`ctx.tool.transform`) *and* onto the wire (`event.tools[TOOL_NAME]` in the context hook with
  its `input` **and** `output` schema) — a tool only on the registry is never available to the
  model, and one called without an `output` schema makes the host reject it. There is no
  `noReply`/agent flag; write-paths return plain output and the user simply is not addressed.
- **The command reads the same measured context** the transform used (the `payloads`
  map), so `/skillstate` cannot disagree with the payload the model is about to receive.
- Traps: tool **output values must be copied** before shipping so a host mutation can't touch
  plugin-owned state (stale after repair); never log tool results (they can impersonate the
  model); `manualCommand: false` removes the command but leaves the tool and the pass intact.
- Trap — the tool's `execute` runs against the **durable** store, so a write from a session
  whose request never reached the context hook still lands (a session created outside a turn).

### Install & uninstall (`scripts/install.ts`)

- **The install is a copy, not a link.** The host discovers a plugin by resolving
  `<root>/server(.ts|.js)` inside `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (user scope) or
  `<project>/.opencode/plugin/` (project scope). Nothing else is required: no global config
  entry, no build step, no dependency to install — the package has zero runtime
  dependencies, so a copy needs no `node_modules`. So the installer's whole job is to place
  a copy of the shippable set in the right directory, which is why it is a script rather
  than a package manifest.
- **The copy beats the link on every axis that survives a restart.** The host imports the
  plugin's module graph once per process, so a link and a copy are equally live only after a
  restart — the old claim that an edit to `src/` is live on the next request was never true
  (the installer's own `--help` has always said "A code change needs an OpenCode restart").
  What the copy adds: the install is a real directory in the shape a user gets, it cannot
  break because a working tree moved, and it can be **compared** against the repository, so
  a stale install is diagnosable drift rather than a plugin quietly running old code.
- **The shipped set is read from the manifest.** `shippableFiles(root)` reads `package.json`'s
  `files[]` and always appends `package.json` itself — `"type": "module"` is what makes the
  host load the `.ts` as ESM, and a copy without its manifest fails to load. Every entry is
  checked against the tree, so a manifest listing a missing file is an install-time error
  rather than a silently incomplete copy.
- **Idempotence is measured on bytes.** `installInto` compares `sha256` hashes first: a copy
  matching the shipped set exactly is left alone (`action: "current"`, nothing written); a
  drifted copy is replaced wholesale (`"updated"`), because a reinstall is an upgrade.
  `driftReport(path, root)` names what differs — `missing`, `changed`, `extra` — which is the
  diagnostic a link could never give, since a junction always agreed with itself.
- **Trap — an old install is a junction, and a junction is deleted without recursion.** The
  installs in both scopes were junctions to the repo root before the copy switch, and they
  are still there until the first reinstall. `removeLink` uses `lstatSync` to tell a link
  from a real directory and issues a bare `rmSync` for a link: recursing follows the junction
  and deletes the *target's* contents — this repository included. Never `Remove-Item
  -Recurse` one by hand. A real directory is deleted with the recursive form, which is safe
  because no link is followed.
- **Trap — a drifted copy is a real state, not a broken one.** `--status` reports a junction
  as "from before the copy switch; install replaces it", and a copy as in-sync or drifted
  with named counts. A drifted copy installs fine and runs old code; the fix is a reinstall,
  not a hunt for the reason discovery stopped working.
- **A code change needs a restart.** The host does not watch module files; the plugin row is
  resolved once per server process. `plugin:status` reports what the *filesystem* says, which
  is why it can disagree with a running host that has not re-scanned. See the restart trap in
  `HANDOFF.md`.
- **npm swallows flags.** `npm run plugin:uninstall -- --project` — without the second `--`,
  `--project` is consumed by npm and never reaches the script.

## Config keys / UI

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch — off returns the disposer before any registration |
| `nudgeWhenStale` | `true` | remind the model to update Σ after a stretch with no new instruction |
| `staleAfter` | `8` | steps with no new user message before the nudge |
| `manualCommand` | `true` | expose `/skillstate` |
| `sigmaWarnTokens` | `16000` | print a Σ size line in `/skillstate` when Σ's own render passes this many tokens, **and fold Σ** when a write pushes it past the same line; `0` disables both |
| `sigmaCondenseChars` | `400` | fold a finding longer than this into its head and tail, keeping the full text in the session archive; `0` disables the fold |

`sigmaWarnTokens` and `sigmaCondenseChars` are the two keys this page owns that the
transform does not read: they shape the report's size line and the write path's fold,
and nothing in the context pass consults either. The gate is deliberately the same
threshold as the line — the line names the pressure and the fold is what answers it,
so a model is told and then helped rather than quietly edited. Measured from the store
on three live sessions, a 400-character floor removes 17.6K, 13.3K and 7.5K tokens of Σ.
The first session it then ran on for real shed 10,483 tokens (41,932 characters) at the
same floor, less than the 17.6K projected for it because a folded finding still costs its
head, its tail and a marker; a re-run over that Σ folds nothing at all.

## Tests that pin it

`scripts/smoke.mjs` — the `skill_state` ack (`updated → step 5 (changed: objective, findings,
step) · dropped (not in the schema): not_a_key`), **the durable write** it persists, the
**string-tolerant read** (the schema admits `["object", "string"]`; a bare and a fenced JSON
string both write and the ack says the string was parsed; a broken string and a non-object
string refuse with Σ and the step untouched), `/skillstate` prints Σ + the per-turn index,
`/skillstate now` forces a pass leaving pairs intact, stale reminder appended only at a
balanced tail, the **Σ size line** past `sigmaWarnTokens` and its silence below it — and,
in the same report, that line naming the archive and `/skillstate <key>` once a fold has
put something in it — the **fold** (one long finding folded to head and tail, a correction
and a two-of-three series superseded, the marker naming exactly what left, the archive
holding every character of it, and the size line then silent because what it complained
about is gone), its **idempotence** (a second write leaves the findings and the archive
byte-identical), the **archive bound** (a finding larger than the bound entire: the newest
fold survives and the oldest entry yields to it), and the **read path** (**skillstate
recall**) — a recalled key returns the *middle* of the folded text that the render does not
have, a superseded key is handed back although Σ no longer holds it, the listing is largest
first with the superseded keys marked, a miss says so rather than throwing, and a session
with no payload still answers, because a recall does not wait for a request the way the
report does.
The **model-side recall** (`skill_state recall`) hands the tool the same read: the *middle* of
a folded key comes back through `execute`, `recall` as `archive` lists what the fold set

# Σ — schema, store, and the ⊕ merge

Status: shipped (v0.2) · Read when: Σ fields; a null that should delete; an unknown key that should be dropped; arrays replace vs merge; seeding from tools; state persistence / restart; render/stability.

User-visible behavior: `docs/SPEC.md` → Scope, Compaction. The state is the sufficient statistic the paper's runtime maintains; see the paper `docs/arXiv-2608.26263v2/acl_latex.tex` source and `DESIGN.md` for the design.

## What it does

- Holds one structured execution state **Σ per session**, durable under
  `state/<sessionID>` in the plugin-scoped KV (`ctx.storage`), with an in-memory LRU
  (`MAX_SESSIONS`) as a **write-through cache** in front of it.
- The **⊕ merge** applied to a `state_patch`: recursive dict merge, a `null` deletes a key at
  any depth, arrays replace wholesale, and **top-level keys the schema does not own are dropped**.
- Seeds `files`/`cwd`/`activeFiles`/`step` from tool calls — **only filling holes**, never
  clobbering model-authored Σ.
- Renders Σ with **canonical key order** so the injected bytes are stable and cacheable.

## Map

- `src/core/schema.ts` — `STATE_FIELDS` / `StateField` (the contract), `merge`
  (⊕; recursive dict merge + null-delete), `validateKeys`, `unknownKeys`, `changedKeys`,
  `fingerprint`, `render` / `orderedValue` (canonical order).
- `src/core/state.ts` — `stateStore(sessionID, { storage, log })` (async: a cache **miss**
  does one `storage.get`, a hit is served from memory), `stateKey`, `PersistedState`
  (`{ state, collapsed, summary }`), `MAX_SESSIONS = 64`, `resetStateStore` / `forgetSession`
  / `stateOf` / `stateCount`, per-session record: `apply`, `set`, `seed` (holes only), `step`
  (reads `Σ.step`), `setCollapsed` / `collapsed`, `setSummary`, `observeUser`, `hydrated`,
  turn memory `turnOf` / `assignTurn` / `highestTurn`.
- `src/core/seed.ts` — `seedHintsFromMessages` (the scan), `seedHints` (the transform's window
  slice), `EMPTY_HINTS`, `SeedHints`; tracks only `trackTools` calls and `glob`-style results.
- `src/core/view.ts` — `valueText`, injected-id helpers (shared with the collapse pass).
- `src/core/types.ts` — `StorageDomain` (the port alias for `ports.Storage`), `CollapsedSpan`, `LastRequest`.

## How & why

- **The schema lives in the runtime, never in the model's head.** The paper's whole defence
  against its two state failure modes — a model *overwriting* a key it did not mean to and one
  *deleting* what it did not own — is a deterministic runtime that validates before applying.
  So: an unknown top-level key is dropped; a `null` deletes; an array replaces (it is never
  element-merged); a plain object merges, so a patch to `files/a` does **not** wipe `files/b`.
- **Base is never mutated** (`merge` starts from `{ ...state }`); a rejected patch leaves Σ
  exactly as it was. The merge itself stays synchronous: load, merge, persist.
- **`step` lives inside Σ** (`Σ.step`), so a step the seed or a prior write set continues
  rather than restarting — the counter is a key, not a private tally.
- **Render is canonical** (schema order for known keys, then alphabetical; nested dict keys
  sorted) so two renders of the same Σ are byte-identical — the property idempotence and
  provider prefix caching both depend on.

### Durability

- **Write-through, and reads are async.** `apply`/`set`/`seed`/`setCollapsed`/`setSummary` each
  `await storage.set` after the in-memory write, so the state a pass is holding is never a
  draft the store never saw. `seed` skips the write when it filled nothing.
- **Degradation is a mode, not a failure.** No store, a refused `get`, a refused `set`, or a
  malformed value all leave the session running in memory; the reason goes to the log under
  `debug`. What it must never do is throw.
- **What survives a restart:** Σ, the committed span and the model's note. What does not: turn
  numbering, which is re-derived from the payload each pass, and `stepsSinceUser`.

### Traps

- **A record captures the storage handle at creation.** One plugin instance per process, so this
  is invisible in practice, but two hosts in one process do not share a store.
- **Arrays replace, and only the current-state keys are arrays.** `plan`/`done`/`open` are
  replaced wholesale by a patch; the model must send the full new list, not a delta. The
  accumulated logs — `findings`/`decisions`/`errors_tried` — are **maps**, so a later write
  merges key by key and an entry made yesterday survives a patch that does not mention it.
  Both shapes are pinned by the smoke test.
- Trap — **`kind` is declarative, not a validator.** `STATE_FIELDS.kind` documents each
  key's shape and `merge` never rejects a mismatch, so a wrong-shaped write passes silently.
  The *hints* are the contract the model actually reads, which is why every hint names its
  own shape (`name -> …` for a map, `a list:` for an array) — when one is ambiguous the
  model drifts, which is exactly how this trap was found.

# mega-skillstate — design contract

> Applies the **SKILL.state** runtime idea (see `docs/arXiv-2608.26263v2/acl_latex.tex`)
> to OpenCode 2.0: bound the context window with an **explicit structured execution
> state Σ** instead of an append-only conversation history.
>
> This project is not about re-verifying the paper; it implements the *context-window
> management* ideas from it on top of the real OpenCode CLI.

## The idea, and the honest mapping

**Paper:** at step *t* the model sees only `A_t = (P, Σ_t, O_t)` — the immutable
procedural spec `P`, a structured execution state `Σ_t`, and the latest observation
`O_t`. The model emits `(R_t, ΔΣ_t, a_t)`; the runtime *validates* then applies
`Σ_{t+1} = Σ_t ⊕ ΔΣ_t` (dictionary merge, **null deletes a key**), and **discards the
reasoning trace `R_t` forever**. Prompt stays `O(1)`, cumulative tokens `O(T)` not `O(T²)`.

**OpenCode reality (v2.0.26):** the model is a tool-use agent. The host rebuilds the
full durable transcript as `event.messages` on *every* request, and the outbound
messages must keep each `tool-call` paired with its `tool-result`. We cannot
synchronously run a private "distiller model" inside the context hook (recursion). So:

| Paper concept | Implementation here |
|---|---|
| `P` (spec + policy) | **static system parts**: a stable, cacheable policy + the Σ-schema + the `skill_state` contract |
| `Σ` (structured state) | a per-session, schema-driven JSON object, **injected** as a message before the recent window |
| `⊕` merge (null deletes) | the merge operator in `state.ts`, applied to model-written `state_patch` |
| `R_t` discarded | the model's *reasoning* is never distilled by the plugin; only what the model commits via `skill_state` survives. Superseded history is dropped from the payload. |
| `O_t` (latest observation) | a **rolling recent window** (`keepRecentTurns`) kept verbatim so the live tool loop stays coherent |
| `O(1)` prompt | the superseded prefix is **collapsed into the Σ message**; outbound payload ≈ `P + Σ + recent window` |
| deterministic runtime validation | `skill_state` validates the patch against the schema (drop unknown keys; keep pairing safe) |

**The one hard constraint, and how we respect it.** The durable transcript is *never*
mutated. A pass rewrites the **outbound payload** only, so the transform is re-derived
on every request from the raw transcript + in-memory Σ. Cuts happen **only at safe turn
boundaries**: never split a `tool-call`/`tool-result` pair, never append inside an open
pair, and (by default) never drop the first user instruction. This is exactly what the
reference plugin proves works on this host.

`types.ts` shapes were measured against the live host.

## Σ schema (default, coding-agent domain; configurable)

```
{
  "objective":      "current sub-goal, one line",
  "plan":           [ { "step": "…", "status": "done|active|todo|blocked" } ],
  "done":           ["completed, one line each"],
  "findings":       { "<name>": "key facts / discovered flags; hypotheses verified or ruled out" },
  "files":          { "<path>": "what we know or did there" },
  "decisions":      { "<name>": "semantic/architectural decision and why, one line each" },
  "errors_tried":   { "<name>": "approach that failed, and why (so it is not repeated)" },
  "working":        { "cwd": "…", "branch": "…", "activeFiles": [<paths>] },
  "open":           ["blockers, open questions, concrete next actions"],
  "step":           <integer current step index>
}
```
(Mirrors the paper's InterCode schema `discovered_flags / tested_hypotheses /
active_files / working_dir / cmd_summary`, re-cut for coding.)

## The `context`-hook transform (the crux — implement exactly)

On each `context` event for session `S`:

1. **Idempotent static policy.** Ensure `event.system` carries P (policy + schema +
   `skill_state` contract). Dedupe by exact-text match so a provider prefix cache stays
   warm (same pattern as the reference's `SECTION_TEXT` push).
2. **Ensure the tool is offered.** If `event.tools["skill_state"]` is absent, add it
   (registry ≠ wire — same lesson the reference documents: a tool only reachable via
   `tool.transform` is never called).
3. **Guard.** If `isChild` (session has `parentID`) and `allowSubagentSessions !== true`, return.
4. **Re-apply from scratch** (durable transcript is raw again): start from
   `event.messages`; drop any previously-injected `skill_state` messages (`mega_` state id).
5. **Measure** `tokens = measureContext(system, messages)`; resolve the model window via
   `model.transform` list (`windowOf`).
6. **Collapse the superseded prefix** (when `collapseOlder` and past any `min`):
   - `view = viewOf(messages)`, `turns = turnsOf(...)`, `balance = balanceCuts(view)`.
   - `keepStartIdx` = first message index at/after turn `currentTurn - keepRecentTurns + 1`
     that is a **safe cut boundary** (`balance.cuts`) and **after** the protected head
     (first real user message, when `protectFirstUserMessage`).
   - The superseded region `(headEnd .. keepStartIdx-1)` is replaced by **one injected
     message** `{ id: "mega_state", role: "user", content:[{type:"text", text}] }` where
     `text` = a clear wrapper + **Σ rendered as compact JSON** + a one-line note naming
     the collapsed turn span. Do **not** collapse the protected head itself.
   - Never split a tool pair: only cut at `balance.cuts`; never append a state/notice
     message while `inFlight > 0` at the tail.
7. **Deterministic seed** (when `seedFromTools`): after collapse, light-scan the kept
   recent window's `tool-call`/`tool-result` parts for `trackTools` to keep
   `working.cwd`, `working.activeFiles`, `files`, `step` minimally current — so Σ tracks
   reality even before the model calls `skill_state`. Seeded keys are *only* filled if
   not already set (never clobber model-authored Σ).
8. **Optional stale nudge:** if `stepsSinceUser` is high and `nudgeWhenStale`, one short
   static-agnostic reminder appended **only at a balanced tail** (`inFlight === 0`).
9. **Never throw.** The whole pass is wrapped so a failure only logs (`debug`) and lets
   the uncollapsed request through.

## `skill_state` tool (the model's write channel — the ⊕ operator)

- `name: "skill_state"`. No reply to the user is generated by a state write.
- `input` schema (zod-shape like the reference `TOOL_INPUT`):
  `{ state_patch: object | JSON string (JSON mutations; **set a key to `null` to delete it**), step?: integer, summary?: string }`.
- The union is deliberate: the host validates the caller's arguments **before** `execute`
  runs, so a quoted JSON string must be admitted there or it is refused with no chance to be
  parsed. `execute` then decodes it — unfence, `JSON.parse`, require a plain object — and
  answers anything else with a soft error that names what arrived; the ack appends a note
  when a string had to be parsed.
- `execute(input, toolCtx)`:
  1. `sessionID = sessionIdOf(toolCtx)`; load per-session Σ.
  2. If `input.step != null`, set `Σ.step`.
  3. `Σ = merge(Σ, state_patch)` — recursive dict merge; a `null` value deletes the key.
  4. **Validate**: keys not in the schema are dropped (runtime owns the schema → guards the
     paper's "Premature State Overwrite / deletion" failure mode). Arrays replace wholesale
     (no deep array merge). Persist Σ, bump step.
  5. Return a compact ack: `textResult("skill-state updated → step N (changed: k1, k2, …)")`.

## Confirmed — the current foundation is valid (do not re-derive)

- Entry (module validator accepts either shape): `export default { id, setup } satisfies Plugin.Plugin`
  (`import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"`), or `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`.
- `setup(ctx) => Cleanup | Promise<Cleanup>`; dispose registrations newest-first.
- **`await ctx.session.hook("context", (event) => { … })` → `{ dispose }`.** `event =
  { sessionID, agent, model, system: SystemPart[], messages: Message[], options, tools }`.
  **Mutating `event.messages` / `event.system` (and `options`, `tools`) in place changes the
  outgoing call only — the durable transcript is never touched**, so re-apply every request.
  Fires on the agent loop *including* tool continuations.
- Message (LLM layer, `Message[]`): `{ id?, role: "system"|"user"|"assistant"|"tool", content: ContentPart[] }`.
  Parts: `{type:"text",text}`, `{type:"reasoning",text}`, `{type:"tool-call",id,name,input}`,
  `{type:"tool-result",id,name,result:{type,value}}`. `SystemPart = {type:"text",text}`.
- `ctx.tool.transform(ed => ed.add(def))`, `ctx.command.transform(ed => ed.add(def))`,
  `ctx.model.transform(ed => ed.list())` (each `{id, providerID, limit:{context}}`).
- `ctx.session.{prompt, compact, get, context, create, …}` — the 15-method domain.
  NOTE field renames docs-vs-source (we don't use them, listed for completeness):
  `session.command` field is `name`; `session.interrupt` field is `resume`.

## Integrate next — upgrades surfaced by lib-1 (the real SKILL.state centrepiece)

1. **Durable Σ via `ctx.storage`.** `ctx.storage.{get,set,remove,scan}` — plugin-scoped,
   durable KV namespaced by plugin id. Replace the in-memory `SessionRecord` store with a
   `ctx.storage` insert + in-memory LRU cache. Key by session (e.g. `state/<sessionID>`).
   Async → `await` in the context hook. *This is the difference between "re-expands on
   restart" and a true persistent execution state.*
2. **Own the distillation via the `compaction` hook.** `await ctx.session.hook("compaction",
   (event) => { … })`. `event` carries the transcript being summarised and a **mutable
   `result`**: setting `event.result = { summary }` **skips the host's summary model call
   entirely** and your string is persisted as the compaction message. This is where Σ is
   distilled, persisted (`ctx.storage.set`), and fed back as `render(Σ)` — the real
   "project reasoning into structured state, then discard the transcript" step. Without it
   we only have the model-written `skill_state` tool + deterministic collapse.
   The hook also exposes `event.messages` (same shape as `context`).
3. **Σ injection primitive — `Message.system()`.** `import { Message } from "@opencode/ai"`;
   `Message.system(content)` → a `{ role: "system", content:[…] }` message you can place at a
   chosen index in `event.messages`, distinct from the `event.system` preamble. Cleaner than
   the `fmac_`-id **user**-role injection the reference plugin uses (that works too — it runs
   on this host — so this is a choice, see "Open design decisions").
4. **Flush before idle via `ctx.event.subscribe({ signal })`.** async iterator over a tagged
   union keyed on `type`; e.g. `session.execution.succeeded` / `.failed` / `.interrupted`.
   Abort in the returned cleanup. (Optional.) Nudge the model to commit `skill_state`, or
   flush a derived Σ, when a session goes idle.
5. **Durable injected turn (optional):** `ctx.session.synthetic({ sessionID, text, description })`
   persists a `[Synthetic context]: …` model-visible turn — if Σ should also show up in the
   transcript, not just the outbound payload.

## Data model nuance

- Two layers. Persisted transcript = `SessionMessage.Info[]` (from
  `ctx.session.context({sessionID})`); the LLM request = `Message[]`. **Inside the `context`/
  `compaction` hooks `event.messages` is already the projected `Message[]`** — no
  `Assistant.cost/tokens/retry` there. If needed, read `ctx.session.context` separately.
- Parts are **not** independently addressable in v2 (no `part.update/remove`); they live
  inside assistant `content`. A tool call is `{type:"tool-call", id, name, input}` paired with
  `{type:"tool-result", id, name, result}` by `id` — our pairing-safety rule stays.
- There is **no `step-start`** part type; synthetic faces are text/media/tool-call/tool-result/
  reasoning/compaction/effort.

## Gotchas that bite

- **Host auto-compaction threshold is NOT tunable from a plugin** (`auto`/`buffer`/`keep` are
  internal). We bound the context ourselves in the `context` hook and *own* the compaction
  *result* via the hook — that's the levers we do have.
- Native (provider-side) compaction bypasses our `compaction` hook's message edits on the
  "summarize older" step; `event.result` still applies. Edge case.
- Hooks run in **registration order**; a later plugin's edits are what an earlier one sees.
  Register early.
- When history must be flattened, the compaction hook's edits to the *existing* summary
  message can be dropped — persist Σ to `ctx.storage` so we re-derive, don't rely on in-place
  edits to the prior summary surviving.
- `ctx.event.subscribe` must be aborted in `setup`'s returned cleanup.
- Discovery dirs for a local plugin: **`.opencode/plugin/` and `.opencode/plugins/`** (both).
  Loader resolves `<root>/server` then `<root>/index` (`.ts` before `.js`); `package.json`
  `exports` (`.`, `./server`) honoured. Resolution never executes plugin code.

## Built-in recap template (overlaps our Σ — reconcile naming)

v2.0's default summary prompt already asks the model for: **Objective / Requirements /
Decisions / Work State (Completed/Active/Blocked) / Next Move / Relevant Files / Important
Context.** This maps closely onto our Σ schema (`objective`/`done`/`active`/`decisions`/
`working.activeFiles`/`open`). When we `set event.result` ourselves we skip it, but if we
ever co-exist, keep our field names aligned so a compaction message reads the same either way.

## Open design decisions (resolve in the integration pass)

- Injection **role**: keep the host-proven **user**-role injected Σ message (prefix `mega_`;
  the reference plugin's `fmac_` pattern, pairing-safe with `inFlight === 0` tail rule) vs
  switch to the semantically-cleaner `Message.system()`. Decide by what inserts cleanly between a protected
  user head and a rolling tool-paired recent window without breaking role ordering.
- **Σ store**: `ctx.storage` + LRU cache vs LRU-only. Recommend `ctx.storage` + LRU cache.
- Whether `/skillstate` and the `skill_state` tool remain the model's write channel, or the
  `compaction` hook becomes the sole distiller (recommend: both — tool for live in-session
  patches, compaction hook for the periodic/whole-history distillation + persistence).

## F1 — Deterministic hard failure: `summary: undefined` in the tool result

**Severity: critical. Reproduced live. A write "fails" but has already persisted.**

- **Symptom** (host error, whole call marked failed):
  `Tool returned a non-JSON value for its output schema: Expected JSON value`.
- **Trigger.** The declared output is `TOOL_OUTPUT = { type: "object", … }`
  (`src/core/skill-state.ts`). `writeSkillState` builds
  `output.summary = record.summary()` (repo `src/core/skill-state.ts:222`; same line
  in the pre-extraction installed copy at
  `src/adapters/opencode/tool.ts:192`). `record.summary()` is `string | undefined`
  (`src/core/state.ts`), and it is `undefined` until some write passes a `summary`
  argument — or after a write clears it with `summary: ""`. An `undefined` leaf is
  not JSON, and the host rejects the whole result.
- **Who hit it, and why others escaped.** The trigger is simply: *a write while no
  summary has ever been set.* PLO1's first call (`seq 113`) and the refactor
  session's first call (`seq 122`) both passed `summary` — so both sessions never
  saw this error once. This session's first two calls (`seq 89`, `seq 98`) passed no
  `summary` and both failed; the third call passed `summary: "probe"` and succeeded,
  after which every no-summary write was fine. The adb session made exactly three
  `skill_state` calls in its whole life — all three without a summary, all three
  failed, and none of its intended state was ever accepted. **A fresh session whose
  model omits the optional summary on its first write burns every write until it
  happens to pass one** — the common case, since the summary is described as
  optional.
- **Live reproduction (this session, 2026-10-13).** With a summary present, writes
  succeed. A call that clears it (`summary: ""`) returned exactly
  `Tool returned a non-JSON value for its output schema: Expected JSON value`; the
  very next call, carrying a summary again, succeeded. The store shows the
  failed clear had already taken effect (`summary` gone, step advanced) —
  see "phantom write" below.
- **Phantom write (second bug inside the first).** Validation happens *after*
  `execute` has merged and persisted, so this class reports failure while the write
  has landed. Confirmed twice:
  1. This session's `seq 89` errored, yet the current Σ still contains that patch's
     `files` and `open` values, which were never re-sent;
  2. the clear-test call errored, yet `kv` shows its `summary` clear and step bump
     persisted.
  Consequence: a model that reads the error as "nothing was written" re-sends the
  same patch (wasted call, confusion, occasional duplicate "changed: none" acks) —
  while the record silently moved.
- **Fix (one line, plus a pin).** In `writeSkillState`, either
  `summary: record.summary() ?? null` or omit the `summary` key when `undefined`.
  Add a smoke pin: a write with no summary must produce an output with no
  `undefined` leaf (assert `output.summary` is absent or `null`). Apply the same
  line in the installed copy's `tool.ts` **or** reinstall (`npm run plugin:install`
  and `npm run plugin:install:project`) and restart the host; the host resolves the
  plugin once per process.
- **Open question.** Whether the host's rejection could also be avoided by a
  stricter `TOOL_OUTPUT` — no: the schema is already permissive; the value itself is
  the problem. The `?? null` fix is the minimal correct one.

## F2 — Soft refusals: `state_patch` sent as a malformed JSON string (29 calls)

**Severity: high-frequency friction (4.5% of all calls). No data loss recorded, but
retries cost calls and once shortened a finding.**

- **Symptom** (soft refusal; Σ untouched; call marked *completed*):
  `state_patch arrived as a string that is not valid JSON; nothing was written. Pass
  the object itself, not a quoted or fenced copy.`
- **Taxonomy of all 29 recorded strings** (parse-tested against Node's `JSON.parse`;
  archived in `tool-calls.json`):
  | class | n | shape |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | extra trailing `}` | **26** | one closing brace too many after an otherwise valid object (`…"}}` for a patch that ends `"}`), incl. strings that double-wrap the whole call as `{"state_patch": {…}}` |
  | unclosed / truncated | 2 | parse ends mid-structure (`Expected ',' or '}' … at position <end>`) |
  | quote-shifted key | 1 | `"execution_policy_note: \"…\"` (seq 7504) |
- **The double-wrap sub-family.** Four string patches parsed as valid JSON whose only
  top-level key was `state_patch` — the merge dropped it and the ack said
  `dropped (not in the schema): state_patch` with `changed: none` (e.g. retry of
  `seq 6573`). Same model confusion as the refusal, one brace away from it.
- **Retry behaviour.** 27 of 29 recovered on the very next `skill_state` call —
  but the cost is real: one cluster (`seq 7970/7977/7992`) failed three times, and
  the eventual success for that content (`seq 7999`) carried only the step; the
  model then re-wrote the finding **shortened** (`seq 8008`). Detail degradation
  after a refusal is the concrete loss channel.
- **What the models understood.** Most modelled the refusal as a size or quoting
  problem and retried "smaller" — e.g. seq 2792: "maybe because of the colon inside
  the string…"; seq 5685: "maybe the harness serialized it wrong, or my JSON had a
  problem." The message names the payload but not the defect, so the retry is a coin
  flip. The refactor session's later reasoning shows the learning stuck ("the
  state_patch must be an object… I'll pass the object"), and the retry succeeded.
- **Fixes, ranked:**
  1. **Enrich the refusal** (cheap, certain): include the parse error and character
     position, plus a short tail of what arrived — e.g. *"parse failed at char 146:
     unexpected '}' after the end of the value; the string ends `…"arm"}}` — you
     likely added one closing brace too many."* Models fix precise errors; they
     cannot fix a diagnosis-free refusal. `parsePatch`'s `catch` in
     `src/core/skill-state.ts` is the one place to change.
  2. **Tolerant repair for the dominant class** (the 26): when `JSON.parse` fails,
     try a single retry after stripping redundant trailing `}` characters (only
     when the remainder parses to a plain object **and** nothing else was dropped);
     accept and say so in the ack (`note: repaired — one trailing "}" removed`), so
     the correction is visible and teaches the model, exactly like the existing
     `fromString` note. Validate against all 29 archived strings; anything that
     would lose content still refuses. Do not attempt repair for the truncated
     class — that is where silent content loss would hide.
  3. **Tool-description tweak**: reinforce "pass the object itself"; if a string is
     unavoidable, "it must be the exact object JSON — no extra closing brace, no
     wrapper". (`toolDescription()` in `src/core/prompts.ts`.)
- **Already good:** the refusal never touches Σ (parse precedes the store), and the
  union-typed `state_patch` input is what keeps these calls inside the plugin rather
  than at the host gate — keep both.

## F3 — Host argument-gate rejection: `step` fused with the payload (1 call)

**Severity: medium (rare, but the whole call is lost before the plugin runs).**

- Refactor `seq 3266`: the model emitted `step` as a string that had swallowed the
  rest of the JSON — host error:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "skill_state": - step: Expected number` (arguments
  showed `"106,\n\"state_patch\": {…}`). Because the host validates before `execute`,
  the plugin never sees the call and **nothing is written** (no phantom write here).
  The model re-sent it correctly on the next call, and its own note ("arrived as a
  mangled string, so nothing was written") matched the truth for this class.
- **Fix option:** widen `step` to `{ type: ["integer", "string"] }` (the same union
  trick `state_patch` already uses to cross the host gate) and in `writeSkillState`
  accept a pure-integer string; if the string contains `"state_patch"`, return a
  precise soft refusal (*"step must be its own integer argument; your patch appears
  fused into `step`"*) or, optionally, recover the fused patch when it parses.
  Low priority relative to F1/F2, but cheap.

## F4 — Objective quality: model-authored garble and stale objectives

**Severity: medium (record hygiene; a garbled objective misleads every later
request until someone fixes it). No runtime corruption was found.**

- **The garble (PLO1).** `seq 9452` wrote:
  `"tray lib.rs: ShellExecuteW open helper DONE; next TrayAction::CheckUpdate (…);
  ShellExecuteW open helper; read 60-110 shows TrayAction 66-73, …"` — a blend of
  the new sentence and the tail of the previous objective (the phrase repeats; the
  line numbers are stale). One nudge-review later the model read Σ back, judged it
  "slightly garbled (repeats itself)", and rewrote it clean (`seq 9461`, same
  message). The failure mode is patch composition: rewriting a long objective by
  gluing text, with no length or duplication guard anywhere in the loop.
- **Stale/contradictory objectives (refactor).** `seq 1035`: objective still
  "Done — coffee/FUNDING change committed…" when the work had not been committed;
  `seq 3100`: objective said "remaining: update the 5 feature pages… then commit"
  while `done` already carried commit `9a2be0a` — the model noticed the
  contradiction and patched both. A third note (`seq 1163`) is the model reasoning
  about **how much to trust Σ** ("error result → don't believe the nearby `done`") —
  trust heuristics forming by hand where the runtime offers no signal.
- **Optimizations (warn, never reject — the schema owns shape, not content):**
  1. **Objective lint in the ack.** After a write, run a deterministic check on
     `state.objective`: repeated substrings (e.g. any ≥24-char segment occurring
     twice), length ≥ ~200 chars, newline present, or `next/remaining` phrasing
     while every `plan` item is `done`. Append one line to `ackText` output:
     `objective note: repeats a phrase — consider rewriting it as one short line`.
     The ack is the loop the model already reads; this is where it can learn.
  2. **Guidance.** In `toolDescription`/policy, say explicitly: keep `objective` a
     short *current* goal; put detail in `plan`/`findings`; rewrite it, don't append
     to it.
  3. Optional: `nudgeText` asks for a one-line "does `objective` still describe the
     current goal?" review — the PLO1 garble survived until exactly such a review
     happened by accident.

## F5 — Ack semantics are ambiguous

**Severity: low, but it compounds — the ack is the model's feedback loop.**

- **`(changed: none)`** (≥9 in PLO1): indistinguishable between "your values were
  identical to what was already there" (correct no-op), "your write landed but the
  host reported failure" (F1 phantom case, where no ack is ever delivered at all),
  and "you passed the same `step` again, nothing else new". Examples where the
  model then re-patched defensively: `seq 8647`, `8764`, `9058` (step-only writes
  that equalled the current step).
- **Same-step consecutive acks**: 21 of 502 PLO1 ack pairs report the same step
  twice in a row (e.g. `step 286 (changed: step)` then `step 286 (changed: plan,
  findings, open)`), because the model re-passed the current step number. Refactor:
  0 of 111. Reads like a lost increment.
- **Proposal:** ack phrasing that names the situation, e.g.
  `changed: none (values already identical)` and `step 286 (kept; not set this
  write)` vs `step → 287 (set)`. Purely additive text in `ackText`
  (`src/core/prompts.ts`); no schema change.

## F6 — Σ growth: 119 KB state in PLO1

**Severity: medium design risk; needs a decision, not an emergency fix.**

- `kv` sizes: PLO1 **118,979 bytes** at step 485 (524 steps of findings-heavy work);

  (`stateMessageText` → `render(state)`) carries the whole state on every request,
  so the bounded-context promise erodes exactly on the long sessions it matters for.
- Options: (a) a threshold line in the ack (`Σ is ~30k tokens; consolidate
  findings`); (b) guidance to move resolved items out of `findings`; (c) a
  per-key/per-value cap convention in the schema hints; (d) a deliberate design
  pass on condensation (kept out of scope here). Recommend measuring the injected
  payload at a few sizes before choosing.

- Hash comparison (2026-10-13): `src/adapters/opencode/index.ts` identical in both

# mega-skillstate — Roadmap (portability)

**Status:** active, Phase 3 all but closed. Phases 1 (core extraction, `9a2be0a`)
and 2 (Pi adapter, through `51adc29`) are landed and gated green; Phase 3's file
set (daemon, codecs, session identity, store, MCP server, config, setup docs) is
landed, and the only part left is the live manual runs on Claude Code and Codex.
**Decided (2026-10-10, user):** Tier 2 (Claude Code / Codex) goes through a
**wire-level proxy daemon** (full fidelity). Hooks-only degraded mode is a
fallback only, not a route.

> This is a **plan**, not a description of the code: `docs/features/` is the
> mechanism, `docs/SPEC.md` the user-visible behavior, `AGENTS.md` the process.
> Phases here become feature pages as they land.

## 1. Goal

Run the plugin's core on four targets:

| Target | Tier | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | 1 — native | existing `context` hook (baseline, adapter #0, no behavior change) |
| Pi (earendil-works/pi) | 1 — native | `context` event (request-local) + `registerTool` + `appendEntry` |
| DeepSeek Harness | 1 — native | durable **surface replacement** (no request seam exists by design) |
| Claude Code + Codex | 2 — proxy | one local daemon: request rewriter + MCP server + shared Σ store |

And establish the rule that **future features are core-only changes**. Adapters
are touched only when a feature needs a capability the port interface does not
expose — interface growth, once per adapter, small and mechanical.

## 2. Why the proxy for Tier 2

- Claude Code hooks cannot rewrite conversation history (`PreCompact` can block
  but cannot inject — issues #46191 / #50682); Codex hooks likewise cannot
  touch the payload. A proxy behind `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` /
  `model_providers.<id>.base_url` gets the exact same "rewrite the outbound
  request, never the transcript" seam the in-process adapters use.
- One daemon serves both hosts and also carries `skill_state` over MCP (stdio +
  streamable HTTP) — so the tool works even where only MCP is wired up.
- Codex caveat, documented, not blocking: ChatGPT-subscription auth does not
  route through custom providers; the proxy requires the API-key route. The
  hooks-only degraded mode (Σ injection, no collapse) is the documented
  fallback there.

## 3. Target architecture

```
src/
  core/                  pure, host-free
    schema.ts            Σ schema + ⊕ merge (null-delete, unknown-key drop)
    state.ts             per-session state logic (over the Storage port)
    seed.ts              derived floor from tracked call arguments
    view.ts              turn numbering, safe cuts, call/result pairing balance
    prompts.ts           section / nudge / ack / report text
    context.ts           the host-free transform: applyTransform, describeContext
    skill-state.ts       the write semantics both hosts' tools wrap
    skill-state-command.ts  the pure half of the command's report
    compaction.ts        the compaction seam (duck-typed CompactionEvent)
    config.ts            resolveOptions / resolveConfig / resolveThresholds
    types.ts             minimal core message/part vocabulary
    ports.ts             the six port interfaces
  adapters/
    opencode/            context hook, skill_state tool, command, StorageDomain
    pi/                  context event, registerTool, registerCommand, appendEntry
    dsh/                 surface replacement, ctx.tools.register, command, session events
  proxy/
    server.ts            HTTP reverse proxy, SSE passthrough (never buffers streams)
    codec-anthropic.ts   Messages API ↔ core vocabulary
    codec-openai.ts      Responses API ↔ core vocabulary
    mcp.ts               skill_state MCP server (shares the store)
    store.ts             durable Σ store (SQLite), session identity mapping
    config.ts            port, upstreams, thresholds (mirrors options.json), debug
```

The six ports (keep them coarse — six, not sixty):

1. `CollapseStrategy` — `request-rewrite` (OpenCode, Pi, proxy) or
   `surface-replacement` (DSH)
2. `Codec` — host parts ↔ core vocabulary; strip/restore opaque content
3. `Storage` — durable per-session Σ
4. `ToolBridge` — register a tool with schema + handler
5. `CommandBridge` — register a command + reply channel
6. `SessionLifecycle` — session identity, init, dispose

Rules: no host conditionals in core; the port interface grows only by adding a
method; adapters translate decisions, they do not implement features.

or async init, and jiti loads the TypeScript directly — no build step. So the
adapter's entry is a factory, not `setup(ctx)` + a disposable: `registerTool` and

unsubscribe `() => void`, which is the only lifetime the factory holds.

1. `CollapseStrategy` → `pi.on("context")`. The handler rewrites **by return** —

   branch-aware and resume-safe, so Pi never uses the KV blob at all. This is

## 10. Payload erosion — what shipped, and what the measurement actually said

A live `/skillstate now` reported `context 417369 -> 458371 tokens` with "Σ
already stands for turns 2-18; nothing left to collapse this pass" — a
41,002-token **increase** on a pass that folded nothing. The reply's third line,
"the next request carries the collapsed payload", was untrue on that pass and was
removed in `82f9d1c`; the erosion itself shipped in `beeb72f` and is recorded
here, because the measurement that decided it corrected the one this section
previously carried. The same command again, now that the erosion is installed,
is recorded under *What the erosion bought, measured live* below.

### What the live number decomposes into

`tokensBefore` excludes Σ — the pass strips the injected message first — so the
458,371-token payload is **~417K kept window + ~41K Σ**. That Σ figure is not a
constant: it was ~164K chars at the reading and had grown to ~224K chars by the
time it was measured again. Σ is injected into *every* request, so its growth is
the one erosion the collapse cannot see, because the collapse is turn-gated and
indifferent to how many tokens the state message costs.

### What the window is actually made of

The synthetic probe that priced this section ran `applyTransform` over
transcripts whose tool results were 2,400 to 400,000 chars, and concluded the
kept window was 99-99.9% tool-result value. **That conclusion is wrong about real
sessions.** Measuring the real sessions' kept windows from `opencode.db` (the last
four user turns of PLO1, JEV, phase2 and the refactor session, split by part type
and by tool):

| session | window chars | skill_state patches | reasoning | tool results |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLO1 | 1,257,251 | 38.1% | 31.1% | 21.7% |
| JEV | 475,326 | 51.8% | 24.9% | 11.2% |
| phase2 @ seq 8147 | 1,799,318 | 44.6% | 32.8% | 11.2% |
| refactor | 1,069,130 | 2.4% | 83.8% | 10.0% |

So the two dominant components are the model's **own patch inputs** and
**reasoning** — not tool results, which the synthetic probe had inverted. In PLO1,
tool-call inputs are 44.6% of the window and `skill_state` patches are 85.6% of
those inputs (479,501 of 560,227 chars). Results *are* concentrated in a handful
of huge ones (82-95% of tool-output bytes in results over 2,000 chars), but they
are a minority of the window. The ordering matters: folding patch bodies addresses
the largest component, capping results addresses a smaller one, and Σ's own text
is a third.

### Shipped in `beeb72f`

- **Fold** (`foldPatchInputs`, default on): an old turn's `skill_state` patch body
  becomes a marker naming its keys and byte size. Σ in the same payload already
  renders the merged result and the call's own result says which keys moved, so
  the body is pure redundancy.
- **Cap** (`maxResultChars`, 4000, 0 disables): an old turn's string result over
  the budget becomes head + omission marker + tail; `glob` is exempt because the
  seed extracts its file list from one.
- **Warn** (`sigmaWarnTokens`, 16000, 0 disables): `/skillstate` prints a Σ size
  line naming the dominant key past the threshold, because Σ's own growth is
  charged to every request and the collapse cannot see it.

All three are content-only, ordered as step 7 of `applyTransform` — after the
collapse and the seed, before the nudge — so the seed and the fold-span arithmetic
still read the raw conversation. Both cuts are idempotent by construction (a folded
patch is a string and the fold only rewrites plain objects; a capped value is
already under its budget), and the live turn is never touched. The golden
fixtures did not move, which is the point of keeping them byte-identical.

### What the erosion bought, measured live

The reading that opened this section was taken *before* the erosion shipped. The
same `/skillstate now`, on the same session, now prints `context 66625 ->
125541 tokens` with "Σ already stands for turns 2-47".

- **`tokensBefore` fell 417,369 -> 66,625** — the sixfold cut this section was
  written to find, measured on the live host rather than in a probe. Both
  installed scopes carry `src/core/erosion.ts` byte-identical (SHA `3B97BD94`,
  40 files each), which is what retires F7's "nothing here is live until a
  reinstall" caveat.
- **The collapse advanced from turns 2-18 to turns 2-47** — 29 more turns folded
  since the reading quoted at the top of this section.
- **Σ is now 58,916 tokens, 47% of the payload.** With nothing left to fold, the
  pass removes nothing and re-inserts Σ, so `tokensAfter` exceeds `tokensBefore`
  by Σ's whole size. That delta is a constant rather than a result — the same
  failure family as the third line removed in `82f9d1c` — and it could not fall
  until Σ was condensed. The condenser shipped in `424b719`, the very next
  commit, so the delta now falls by whatever the fold removes:
  41,932 chars, about 10.5K tokens, on the first real session it ran on.

So the saving lives in the comparison between two requests' `tokensBefore`, which
the command never prints side by side, while the printed delta measures only Σ's
price. That is why the next lever was condensation and not another body cut —
and that lever has since shipped (`424b719`).

### What the two-causes table got wrong, and what the correction buys

The table this section carried until `beeb72f` was:

| cause | share of the live 417K | fix |
|---|---|---|
| kept window's tool results | ~90% (~376K) | a result-size threshold the collapse can act on |
| Σ's own accumulated text | ~10% (~41K) | condensation, or a size warning |

It was right that there are two independent causes, and right that fixing only
the smaller one leaves the payload essentially unchanged — which is why the
condensation hypothesis was refuted as the **primary** fix. It was wrong about
which cause was which: the measured windows above say patch inputs are the
largest component and results a minority. So the order of work was inverted, and
the result cap shipped as the second lever rather than the first.

### Σ's own growth, measured rather than probed

`render(Σ)` over the same real sessions, findings-dominated in every one:

| session | Σ total | findings share |
|---|---|---|
| PLO1 | ~189,538 B (~47K tok) | 86.5% |
| phase2 | ~224,341 B (~56K tok) | 79.5% |
| refactor | ~70,775 B (~18K tok) | 64.8% |
| JEV | ~24,447 B (~6K tok) | 25.3% |

So Σ is a real and growing cost in exactly the sessions that use it most, and
the lever that addresses it condenses **findings** rather than the state as a
whole. A `sigmaWarnTokens` line now reports the size in `/skillstate`; the
condenser that follows from it has since shipped (`424b719`) — see *What shipped
since this section was written* below.

### The ordering trap, and why it held

Σ is seeded from exactly the window that will survive and rendered **once** at
injection, so the erosion pass had to sit *after* both — re-deriving its view of
the final payload rather than the pre-collapse one, because a summary computed
over payload the pass was about to rewrite is not the payload the model sees.
Both cuts are idempotent, which is what makes that ordering safe: a folded patch
is a string, a capped value is under its budget, and a second pass can produce
nothing new. This is also why the golden fixtures did not move.

# mega-skillstate — behavior spec

User-visible behavior only: what the product does and what a user sees,
readable without knowing the code. Behavior belongs here even when the code is
where the reason for it lives — the reason, the mechanism and the traps live in
`docs/features/`, and process and hard rules live in `AGENTS.md`.

<!-- One section per user-visible area, in the order a user meets it. State what
happens, then the defaults and limits a user can observe, then what is out of
scope. Name the settings and their values, but not the code that reads them:
the feature page for the area owns the mechanism. -->

## Scope

`mega-skillstate` is an OpenCode 2.0 CLI plugin that manages a session's
context window by carrying an **explicit, structured execution state (Σ)** instead of
the usual ever-growing conversation history.

Once a session has accumulated at least `min` turns, every later request the model
sees is rebuilt from three parts: the plugin's standing policy, the current Σ
(rendered as a compact JSON block placed right after the first user instruction),
and a short **recent window** of the newest `keepRecentTurns` turns kept verbatim.
The turns older than that window are **collapsed into Σ** and dropped from the
outgoing request, so the payload stays roughly constant in size instead of growing
with every turn. The model keeps Σ current by calling the `skill_state` tool and can
read it back with the `/skillstate` command.

It is for long agent sessions where append-only history would otherwise grow
quadratically. In practice, collapsing turns into Σ is **gated by turn count**
(`min` to start, `keepRecentTurns` kept), not by a token budget.

Because the window itself can still be enormous within those turns, the plugin
also **erodes the content of the window's older turns**: a `skill_state` call's
patch body from a turn that is no longer the live one is replaced by a marker
naming the keys it carried (Σ already renders the merged result, and the call's
own result says which keys moved), and a tool result over `maxResultChars` is
reduced to its head and tail with a marker saying how much was omitted. The
**live turn is never touched** — it is the step being taken. Both cuts change
only content, never which messages exist or how a tool call is paired with its
result, so the conversation the model sees stays well formed; folding is
idempotent, because a folded patch body is a string and only a plain object is
ever folded. A `glob` result is exempt, since the file list Σ seeds itself from
is read out of one. Both cuts are user-visible behavior and both have an
explicit off switch (`foldPatchInputs`, `maxResultChars: 0`).

When Σ has grown past `sigmaWarnTokens`, `/skillstate` says so and names the key
that dominates it, because Σ is injected into every request and the collapse is
indifferent to how much that costs. The same threshold is where **Σ is folded**: a
write that finds Σ past it condenses the state's own prose, so whatever made Σ big
stops being charged to every request. Two folds, both decided by a key and never by
reading the prose — a finding whose key is another key plus a correction
(`note_corrected`, `_again`, `_final`) replaces the key it corrects, and a numbered
series (`probe_step3`) keeps only its newest member; and a finding longer than
`sigmaCondenseChars` keeps its head and its tail. What leaves the render is written
to the session's **archive**, inside the same durable record and never rendered, so
the text is recoverable rather than destroyed; the archive is bounded oldest-first
and the newest fold is never the entry dropped. What was set aside reads back by hand:
`/skillstate <key>` prints one archived finding in full — for a folded key that is the
middle its render no longer shows, and for a superseded one it is the only copy left —
while `/skillstate archive` lists the archive, largest first. The model has the same read
inside the tool: `skill_state` with `recall` set to a key prints it in full, and `recall`
as `archive` lists what was set aside, with no write, no step and no payload needed.
Folding is idempotent and inert
below the threshold, so a small session's Σ is left exactly as the model wrote it.
`sigmaCondenseChars: 0` disables it.

## Compaction

When the host needs a compaction message, the plugin answers it with Σ instead of
asking for one. It combines the Σ the model has maintained through `skill_state`
with a deterministic sweep of the transcript (the same `files` / `working` /
`step` floor the collapse uses, filling only keys the model has not written), and
hand that back as the compaction message. If the result has something to say —
an objective, a plan, completed work, findings, files, decisions or open items — the
host makes **no summarization call of its own** and persists that text. If it has
nothing to say, the plugin stays out of the way and the host summarizes as usual.

Σ is **durable**: it is stored per session under the plugin's own storage, so a
restart of the plugin or the host brings the state back instead of re-expanding to
the raw transcript. A failure reaching that store degrades to in-memory state and
is reported in the log; it never breaks a session.

It deliberately does **not**:

- re-verify or reproduce the source paper's results (the paper is a reference,
  not a test target);
- touch the durable transcript — it only rewrites the request the host is about to
  send, and reads (never writes) the transcript handed to the compaction seam;
- run a private model to distill Σ: the state is maintained semantically by the
  model itself, and the deterministic sweep only fills the floor;
- replace the host's own built-in compactor when the distilled Σ is empty;
- handle multi-agent shared state with concurrent writes (a limitation the paper
  itself records);
- act on sub-agent (child) sessions unless `allowSubagentSessions` is turned on.

## Settings

Every setting below is read the same way from any of three sources, most specific
last: the plugin's built-in defaults, the `options.json` an installed copy
carries, and a user-level `~/.config/opencode/mega-skillstate.json` — which is
created on first run with every default in it and never overwritten afterwards.
A source only replaces the keys it sets, so a partial file is fine. An unknown
key, or a file that is not JSON, is an error: the plugin refuses to load rather
than silently keeping a default. A file that cannot be written is reported and
the plugin still runs. Read the package `README.md` for install scope.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `min` | `4` | integer ≥ 0 — **minimum turns** before the superseded prefix is collapsed into Σ |
| `keepRecentTurns` | `4` | integer ≥ 0 — newest turns kept verbatim beside Σ |
| `collapseOlder` | `true` | bool — collapse the superseded prefix into Σ |
| `protectFirstUserMessage` | `true` | bool — never collapse the first user instruction |
| `allowSubagentSessions` | `false` | bool — also manage sub-agent (child) sessions |

| `trackTools` | `["read","edit","write","patch","glob","shell"]` | tool names scanned when seeding |

Controls the model/user touch: the `skill_state` tool (the model writes a
